What we learned from Wafcon 2026
- Published
Cameroon became just the fourth nation to lift the Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) trophy, joining Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea and South Africa as winners, after demolishing Malawi 3-0 in Sunday's final.
The 2026 edition in Morocco can be largely deemed a success - even after it was postponed just 12 days before the finals were initially scheduled to kick off in March.
BBC Sport Africa looks at what we learned from three weeks of competition in Rabat and Casablanca.
Expansion worked
The decision by the Confederation of African Football (Caf) to expand Wafcon to 16 teams was justified although that announcement appeared a bit last-minute, coming as it did midway through a qualifying phase designed to provide 12 sides.
The Indomitable Lionesses, eliminated by Algeria in those qualifiers, were the big beneficiaries of the expansion, advancing to the tournament on the strength of their world ranking before going on to claim the title.
Ivory Coast, who like Cameroon missed the last Wafcon and also reached these finals thanks to their ranking, topped their group before losing to the Algerians in the quarter-finals.
All four semi-finalists booked their places at the 2027 Fifa Women's World Cup, meaning Malawi and the Algerians will make their debut at the global showpiece alongside Cameroon and Morocco.
More high-level matches are required to aid the development of women's football on the continent and, on first viewing, the 16-team Wafcon format looks like it will help.
A more level playing field
Where the 2024 Wafcon saw few upsets, this tournament provided greater competitiveness and several shock results.
Tanzania bridged a gap of 65 places in the world rankings to upset South Africa in the group stage and the 2022 champions then needed a 99th-minute equaliser to salvage a point against Ivory Coast.
Debutants Malawi were the fairy tale story, upsetting 10-time champions Nigeria with a 3-2 win in their opener before seeing off Ghana and Algeria to reach the final.
Their success was built on the attacking prowess of the Chawinga sisters, but the Scorchers will certainly climb from 153rd in the world - and 32nd in Africa - when Fifa updates its rankings.
Zambia were unfortunate not to reach the knockout stage despite amassing six points in Group C, while Mali were eliminated on goal difference after finishing level with Ghana on four points in Group D.
Cape Verde, Egypt and Kenya were the only sides not to win a game, with the North Africans conceding 15 goals and the Harambee Starlets failing to find the back of the net.
There were 90 goals scored in 32 games (excluding the two Women's World Cup play-offs) with the average of 2.81 goals per game an increase on the average of 2.54 from the 2024 edition.
Female coach wins the day
Cameroon's Valentine Nguele became the fifth female coach to lead a side to glory in what was the 14th edition of the finals.
She emulates Clementine Toure (Equatorial Guinea, 2008), Eucharia Uche and Florence Omagbemi (Nigeria in 2010 and 2016 respectively) and Desiree Ellis (South Africa, 2022).
Her achievement is all the more impressive given that she only took over in June.
"We worked as crazy since two months [ago], day and night, and this is the result," Cameroon technical co-ordinator Dimitri Lipoff told the BBC World Service.
"We had no team, nothing was ready. We tried to build a kind of bubble.
"This is an incredible team effort."
Is dominance of Super Falcons over?
Nigeria came into the tournament targeting a record-extending 11th Wafcon title but the inquest into their worst-ever performance will be long-lasting.
The Super Falcons paid the price for failing to win their group as they were eliminated by Cameroon in the quarter-finals. Worse was to come as they fell to a 2-1 defeat by South Africa in their World Cup play-off, meaning Nigeria will be absent from the tournament for the very first time.
The West Africans have relied on talent developed and based abroad for a number of years which has masked a lack of institutional structure in the country.
With Morocco investing heavily in the women's game, champions Cameroon benefitting from $2m in prize money and Algeria, Ghana and Malawi among the sides making strides, Nigeria's place at the summit of the African women's game is no longer assured.
Former striker Desire Oparanozie has called for "a fresh start - a start that evaluates everything" and the four-time Wafcon winner will get her wish as part of a fact-finding committee established by the country's football federation to examine the failure.
The negatives
Attendances at matches not involving home nation Morocco were once again an issue, continuing a trend of all-but empty stadiums from the 2022 and 2024 editions.
The late rearrangement of the finals will have played its part, while the cost of travel around the continent and the requirement for visas are long-ingrained obstacles.
The use of video assistant referee checks could certainly be speeded up, with one inspection at the pitch-side monitor during Cameroon's group win over Mali lasting almost four minutes.
The hosts were the beneficiaries of soft-looking penalty awards late on against both Cameroon in the semi-final and in the third-placed play-off against Algeria.
But the fact that the Atlas Lionesses failed to convert nine of their 13 spot kicks - having three of four in regulation or extra time saved or missed - points to one large improvement Jorge Vilda's side could make as they hunt an elusive first title.
Questions for the future
Morocco have now held the past three Wafcons, but whether the kingdom has the appetite to host again remains to be seen.
No announcement has been made about where or when the 2028 tournament will be staged, with the finals needing to avoid the Los Angeles Olympics from 14 to 31 July that year.
A similar clash with the Paris Games led to Wafcon 2024 being delayed until July 2025. A regular and viable slot in the Fifa calendar needs to be found.
Attention now switches to the preliminaries for LA 2028, which recommence in October and continue in three international windows next year, with 32 sides competing for two coveted places at the Games.
South Africa and Ghana, meanwhile, will enter an inter-confederation qualifier for next year's Women's World Cup.

I Lost the Password to My Password’s Password
Logging in was never supposed to be this complicated.
One afternoon earlier this month, I pulled up to the rec center and realized that I had a problem. It was not the three boisterous tweens in the back seat who were clamoring to be set loose in the basketball gym. It was my parking app. I had somehow gotten logged out of Passport Parking, which has become the only way to pay for a spot in much of my town, and it was demanding a four-digit PIN to let me back in. My first guess drew a warning message in red letters: “Invalid PIN. PIN cannot contain 4 sequential numbers, 2 repeated digits, or the last 4 digits of your phone number.” I searched my trusty password manager, which was supposed to spare me these predicaments, but it came up empty. By that point, the kids had run ahead and piled themselves against the gym door, waiting for me to let them in.
Lately, the process of accessing apps and websites has grown dizzying. “I’m in password hell,” a colleague confided to me recently. “Every login attempt is playing the lottery.” The problem is not just the sheer number of digital accounts, all of which require their own password, ideally unique and unguessable (which usually also means un-memorizable). It’s the pileup of solutions to that problem: all of the different layers of software offering to remember your passwords, the six-digit codes sent to your phone, the authenticator apps, the passkeys.
Browsers and operating systems compete with third-party password managers to generate, store, and autofill your credentials. Most of my logins live in 1Password, but others are stored in Apple’s Passwords app (usually by accident), and still others were created via “single sign-on” features such as those offered by Google and Facebook. I vaguely recall certain apps—Facebook is one—prompting me many years ago to copy down a set of “login recovery codes” that would become extremely important should I ever get locked out of my account. Whatever device I stored them on was probably wiped and sold long ago.
Logins have always been a hassle. In the 1990s, forgetting your password sometimes meant mailing a postcard to your service provider and waiting a week or two for it to mail you a new password. In the early 2010s, hackers learned to steal massive troves of logins and then reuse them on other services to steal people’s identities. Things spiraled from there; services started requiring unique, complex passwords with arbitrary requirements. These days, the user experience of logging in is “probably worse than ever,” Troy Hunt, a cybersecurity expert who runs the website Have I Been Pwned, told me. “There’s just no consistency.”
Password managers promised a way out, but they often don’t work as seamlessly as you might hope. I click to autofill my password somewhere, and a 1Password authorization appears, only for an iCloud Keychain authorization to pop up directly over it, preventing me from clicking on the 1Password one. When I manually enter a login I thought I remembered, my browser prompts me to remember it; only after I hit “Save” (pro tip: Do not do this) does the website inform me that the password was not recognized. Even when you log in successfully, there’s the tedious dance of waiting for a six-digit authorization code to appear on your phone or in your email, which defeats the concept of a single password for everything. And if you’re somewhere without cell service or you’re sharing a login with someone who isn’t around, you might just be out of luck.
All of these steps serve a purpose. At least in theory, each added layer helps prevent hacks and breaches. Erring on the side of safety is worth an amount of inconvenience. At the same time, extra steps can introduce security problems of their own. Last year, Hunt fell for a clever phishing scheme when he clicked a link to log in to his newsletter service. His password manager failed to autofill his information, which should have alerted him that something was wrong, he said. But like the rest of us, he was so used to things not working that he went ahead and manually entered his credentials on a site that turned out to be an impostor, designed to steal and exploit them.
None of these obstacles is insurmountable on its own. My problem with Apple’s native password manager fighting with 1Password, for instance, was eventually solved with a 10-minute foray into the bowels of my device settings. But together, they amount to a near-daily irritant. For the less tech-savvy, the situation can be overwhelming. My recent attempts to help my mother fix her password-storage system—which involved loose-leaf notepad sheets full of hand-scrawled credentials scattered around her house like Easter eggs—consumed the better part of a day. By the end, she had all of her credentials updated, validated, and stored in a password manager, just as the experts have been advising for years. But even then, her preferred browser, Google Chrome, showed no interest in surfacing the credentials we had stashed in Apple’s Keychain. And some websites short-circuited her attempts to log in by prompting her to set up a “passkey,” which she interpreted as meaning that her password had failed and she needed to scrap it and set up a new one.
Cybersecurity experts will tell you that passkeys—which typically entail logging in to apps or websites with a face or fingerprint scan instead of a password—are the future. When they work properly, they’re both painless and secure. “It may get to a point where we’re all using passkeys and we don’t even know we’re using passkeys,” Lorrie Cranor, a computer-science professor at Carnegie Mellon University who researches privacy and cybersecurity, told me. “I just say ‘Log in’ and I smile at it, and it gets my passkey, and I’m logged in.”
But that future isn’t here yet, and in the present, passkeys have added a new layer of frustration. Part of the problem is that virtually no one seems to know what they are. “The fact that even I have trouble explaining them should be a clue,” Cranor said. Her past research on the rollout of two-factor authentication suggests that most people tend to resist new security features for as long as they can. Companies can nudge them, but for websites and apps trying to attract and retain users, pushing people to adopt an unfamiliar authentication technology risks scaring them away.
To further complicate matters, passkeys generally aren’t yet replacing passwords altogether, even on sites that use them. Because many passkeys live on your device, one that works on your phone might not work on your laptop, and one that works on your personal laptop might not work on your office device. So you still need a password that works across devices as a backup. It’s a lot, Dave Lewis, 1Password’s global-security adviser, acknowledged to me in an email. “The problem is cognitive overload,” he said. “All these tools are trying to help, but they don’t always work together intuitively.” Still, he disagreed that the situation has never been worse: “When the alternative was using the same password across dozens of accounts or putting it on a sticky note, the fact that people now have password managers, passkeys, biometrics, and multifactor authentication is a good thing.”
The mess might compound before it improves. Hacking attempts have been multiplying as crooks harness AI tools. Companies are adding even more security layers that make logging in harder, and they are pleading for people to make the switch to passkeys. On the bright side, maybe the seamless biometric future is actually within sight, and all of our login woes will soon be over. Then again, that’s what we were promised with password managers too.

What are the downsides of a mini PC?
Small space means less cooling, which in turn means less sustained power.
Mini PCs have become a popular alternative to full-size desktops and laptops over recent years. Brands like Geekom, Beelink and Minisforum have appeared, almost overnight, with machines that can fit in your hand while offering performance that can sometimes rival their bigger siblings.
The physical footprint of a mini PC is both a blessing and a curse. Mini PCs are designed to be full desktop replacements, but their size means that they can be tricky to upgrade and even harder to keep cool. Before you rush into mini PC ownership, you'll want to consider these downsides.
Limited options for upgrades
Mini PCs can range in price, from ultra-budget to serious AI workstations, but their components don't differ much from what you'd find in a laptop. Like a laptop, these machines aren't really designed to be upgraded. You aren't expected to be able to swap out a motherboard or replace the CPU. In fact, the CPU and GPU are often soldered onto the motherboard. Unless you're handy with a soldering iron, there's no real route forward to switch these out.
If your mini PC can be upgraded at all, it'll usually allow you to swap out the SSD or RAM. Mini PCs typically come with SO-DIMM memory modules, as well as smaller M.2 SSDs, both of which you'll also find in a modern laptop. It isn't always a given that these are components you can replace, though. You'll find mini PCs on sale that feature both soldered memory and storage that prevent any possibility of future upgrades.
By design, you've also got few options for expansion. The limited space inside a mini PC case means it's unlikely that you'll find extra RAM or SSD slots for upgrades. External I/O might be limited, too, with a smaller number of USB ports, for example.
Some mid-tier and better mini PCs come with OCuLink or Thunderbolt USB-C ports that allow you to connect an external GPU inside an enclosure. This won't allow you to upgrade your mini PC directly, but it can give you extra power for gaming or workstation AI requirements, with some loss of performance compared to a desktop PC.
You've also got a longevity issue. Cheap mini PCs aren't running with the most powerful components, so once they're too slow to use effectively, replacing it fully could be your only option.
Cooling and performance can't compare to a desktop PC
For mini PC owners, performance is a matter of compromise and sacrifice. By choosing the smallest form factor, mini PC owners are choosing to own a machine with none of the air-cooling benefits of a bigger desktop. Space is the limiting factor, as sizing down means there's much less space for fans to be able to circulate cooler air in and out. While mini PCs are designed with complex cooling systems to try and offset this, they can only go so far: you're not achieving RTX 5090-level gaming prowess with one.
That's not to say that powerful mini PCs don't exist, powered by CPUs like the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, which offer performance power to rival desktop equivalent CPUs like the AMD Ryzen 9 9950X. These machines may be closing the gap to rival larger desktops for their CPU performance, but the physical limitations remain. It all comes back to raw power. Sustained performance under heavy load means more heat, and more cooling. Mini PCs are at a disadvantage here compared to desktop PCs, which have more fans or liquid cooling to push components harder.
Laptops offer a similar challenge from a build perspective, with cooling and power that's tricky to scale upwards. Like high-end laptops, mini PCs that can deliver high-end performance will get very hot and, as a result, will become very noisy under sustained loads. There's no way around this. Being built inside a mini PC case means it's an even harder job for the machine to stay cool enough to keep running. Traditional liquid cooling isn't a practical option due to the limited space, either.
Admittedly, this isn't as big an issue with low-power mini PCs. The modern, low-end CPUs used in laptops and mini PCs are typically more power efficient, generating less heat simply by using less electrical power. The compromise here, however, is that performance won't compare to a high-end machine.
Mini PCs aren't designed to be user repairable
Building a desktop PC, even inside a smaller case, will leave you with some options for repairability. If the power supply blows up, assuming no other components are damaged, you can swap it out. If the components are damaged, you can replace them, too.
With a mini PC, you don't have the same luxury, as they aren't designed to be repairable in the same way as a desktop PC. Instead, you can treat a mini PC like you would a laptop. Should the CPU or motherboard fail, sourcing a replacement from a retailer will not be an option. Instead, you'll be left to look at your options for repair under warranty or, more likely, just buying a new one.
Mini PCs can be a poor value investment
The Beelink SER5. The Asus ROG NUC 16. These products exist at both extreme ends of the PC hardware market, with the former priced at $389, and the latter priced as high as $4,999. Yet, they're both mini PCs. They fit inside small (or reasonably small) cases, feature mobile-grade components and use less electrical power than a desktop PC.
To match a desktop PC's raw power, or even get close, you'll be paying a premium. $5,000 will still get you an extremely powerful traditional desktop PC with better performance and more room for future upgrades compared to mini PCs like the NUC 16. That's even more important as we see prices going up across the board, thanks to the spiralling costs for RAM and SSDs caused by AI.
This makes the value of investing in a mini PC harder to justify. If you have $5,000 to spend on an Asus ROG NUC 15, or even just $400 to spend on the Beelink SER5, you could choose to buy a laptop or PC from a better-known brand to last you five years or longer, with a better and more robust warranty period. At the lower end of the market, a second-hand desktop might not last as long, but could still be cheaper and faster than a mini PC for the same cost, while budget laptops and PCs exist with similar specs.
Mini PCs designed for the ultra-budget price bracket, around $600 or less, do still exist, even as we see AI forcing prices up. The value you get from these will depend, once again, on compromise. These aren't designed to be hugely powerful, but exist as cheap options for office work and browsing. If you're choosing a mini PC for its price, performance is going to be the biggest potential bottleneck, and something you'll need to consider before you make your purchase.

Does Elliott have a Liverpool future after latest omission?
- Published
It was a little under a month ago when in the bowels of the Yankee Stadium in New York, Harvey Elliott spoke candidly about his emotions after a "tough" loan spell at Aston Villa and why this summer felt like a second chance for Liverpool.
There was a smile on his face when he spoke about his love for the club - the team he has supported since he was a boy - and wanting to be free and enjoying himself again with his football, because he felt like he had not done that enough.
You only had to see Elliott's joy when he came off the bench in Liverpool's friendly against Monaco earlier this month as all four sides of Anfield stood up and applauded to see what it meant.
With a number of senior first-team players absent, Elliott started Liverpool's first friendly under Andoni Iraola in Nashville and again when Liverpool took on Wrexham in New York four days later but as the World Cup contingent returned, the midfielder was benched and where he stood in the squad became clearer.
On the first weekend of the Premier League season, Elliott was left out of the Liverpool squad entirely for their trip to Newcastle and it now looks increasingly likely that the 23-year-old could be on his way out before the transfer window ends.
Liverpool have received no offers for Elliott - who spent last season on loan at Aston Villa - and his exclusion from the squad on Sunday was not transfer related, nor is the midfielder carrying an injury.
Elliott's contract expires next summer and if first-team football is not possible at Liverpool he needs to go somewhere where it is, to avoid another lost season.
In America, Elliott spoke about how we would speak to Iraola at the "right time" and emphasised the need to be "selfish".
"Ultimately, I'm still wanting to be selfish, doing what's right for me," said Elliott. "Whether that's staying here and fighting for my place or potentially going elsewhere, I'm still unsure at the moment until I get some more intel."
Another year on the fringes would be no good for the man who was named player of the tournament when England Under-21s won the European Championship in 2025.
By now, much has been said about his situation at Villa last season which Unai Emery described as "embarrassing" for all involved.
Elliott played only nine games and a total of 277 minutes after Villa decided early on in the campaign that they did not want to trigger an obligation to sign him from Liverpool for £35m if he made 10 appearances.
Those at Villa stressed Elliott's professionalism and his positivity throughout and to his credit, the attacking midfielder returned early to Liverpool for the start of pre-season after a personally-challenging year.
Iraola himself was impressed by his attitude, saying as much in his introductory press conference.
"I've seen him with this eagerness to show himself. He will have a chance during the pre-season. He came one week earlier and I hope we can see him in a good place," said Iraola.
"Last season had to have been very difficult for him as it was a strange situation that meant they [Aston Villa] couldn't let him play."
In effect, the move to Villa wasted a season of Elliott's career even if he was adamant that it was a "learning curve" in a year where Villa won the Europa League.
"I don't wish it upon any other player, because it's not nice at all," Elliott said.
When he left Liverpool last summer, the primary factor was more game-time after making just one Premier League start during Liverpool's title-winning campaign under Arne Slot in 2024-25.
So with a week to go of the transfer window and with further attacking signings expected at Anfield, perhaps the writing is on the wall.
A move lower down the Premier League or somewhere in Europe may be an option.
After all, this is a player who scored the winner for Liverpool at PSG in a year where the Ligue 1 club won the Champions League.
He is neat on the ball and unafraid to take risks - a return of 15 goals and 21 assists for Liverpool, across all competitions, showcases what he can do.
Either way, it is imperative for all involved that Elliott finds somewhere to play football regularly this season because it seems unlikely at Liverpool and at 23, he cannot afford to have a season like last.

Quick Answer
PowerShell commands such as Get-Help, Get-Command, Get-Process, Start-Process, Stop-Process, Get-Service, Stop-Service, Get-Content, Get-ChildItem, Copy-Item, Move-Item, Remove-Item, and Set-Location help you manage apps, services, files, folders, and system tasks faster on Windows.
PowerShell is a Windows program that simplifies system administration. You can use it to perform many system tasks efficiently and automate repetitive ones. However, to do either, you must know the right commands, or cmdlets (command-lets), as PowerShell calls them.
A typical PowerShell cmdlet follows the verb-noun structure, where the noun is the object you want to act on, and the verb is the action you want to perform on it. This makes them predictable and easy to remember.
Here’s a quick reference guide covering all the essential Windows PowerShell commands to help you get started with PowerShell.
Table of Contents
Essential PowerShell Commands for Windows
Get-Help
Get-Help is a handy cmdlet you can use any time you want to learn about a PowerShell concept or command. It shows information for everything from cmdlets and functions to aliases and scripts. Plus, it shows the exact syntax along with all the available parameters to eliminate the need for guesswork.
Syntax:
Get-Help
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Get-Help cmdlet:
- Get-Help Get-Process : Find out what the Get-Process command does
- Get-Help Get-Process -Detailed : Get a detailed description for the Get-Process cmdlet
- Get-Help Get-Process -Online : View a detailed explanation of the command with examples on Microsoft’s official documentation online
If Get-Help doesn’t return any result, try updating it by running:
Update-Help
Get-Command
Get-Command lists all executable commands installed on your computer, including cmdlets, aliases (or shortcuts that point to other commands), and functions (snippets or scripts that perform specific actions). It’s useful when you want to make sure the command you’re trying to use is supported by PowerShell and available on your system.
Syntax:
Get-Command
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Get-Command cmdlet:
- Get-Command -ListImported : Get a list of all commands in the current session
- Get-Command Get-AppLockerPolicy : View information about the Get-AppLockerPolicy cmdlet
- Get-Command -CommandType Alias : List all alias-type executables
- Get-Command *Service* : Get all the service-related executable elements on your system
Get-Process
Get-Process returns a table of all operating system processes (apps or executables) running on your computer locally. For each item in the table, you see the process name, ID, CPU consumption, and a few other details. This makes it really easy to identify which process is consuming significantly more resources, so you can act on it accordingly and free up system resources.
Syntax:
Get-Process
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Get-Process cmdlet:
- Get-Process -Name notepad : Get details about the Notepad process
- Get-Process explorer | Format-List * : Display detailed information about the explorer processes, including all its properties and their values
Stop-Process
Stop-Process allows you to stop one or more running processes on your computer right from the PowerShell window. To use it, you need the process name or the process ID (or PID), which you can identify by running the Get-Process command.
Syntax:
Stop-Process
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Stop-Process cmdlet:
- Stop-Process -Name notepad : Close the Notepad app
- Stop-Process -Name notepad -F : Force close Notepad
- Stop-Process -Id 3380 : Close the app with a PID of 3380
Start-Process
Start-Process is a PowerShell command that lets you launch one or more processes (or apps) on your computer. You can even open an executable file using it. Start-Process also gives you the ability to choose how you want to start a process. For instance, you may start a program as an administrator or open specific files with their default apps.
Syntax:
Start-Process
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Start-Process cmdlet:
- Start-Process notepad.exe : Launch the Notepad app
- Start-Process -FilePath “notepad” -Wait -WindowStyle Maximized : Open Notepad in a maximized window
- Start-Process -FilePath “sort.exe” : Start a process that uses the sort.exe file
- Start-Process -FilePath “powershell” -Verb RunAs : Open PowerShell as an administrator
Get-Service
Get-Service retrieves and gives you the status of all Windows services running on your computer. It’s useful when you want to identify the status of background services.
Syntax:
Get-Service
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Get-Command cmdlet:
- Get-Service -Name wuauserv : Check the status of the Windows Update service
- Get-Service | Where-Object {$_.Status -eq "Running"} : Filter services to only view the ones that are currently running
Stop-Service
The Stop-Service PowerShell cmdlet lets you stop a system service. You’d typically use it after you’ve run the Get-Service command and identified the problematic service running in the background.
Syntax:
Stop-Service -Name
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Stop-Service cmdlet:
- Stop-Service -Name wuauserv : Stop the Windows Update service
- Stop-Service -DisplayName “telnet” | Stop-Service : Stop a service using its display name
- Stop-Service -Name Spooler -Force : Stop the Spooler service along with other dependent services
Get-Content
Get-Content helps you read the contents of an item within the PowerShell window. You’d mostly use it to get the contents of a file. All you need to do is specify the file and its location. You can even mention the number of lines in the file you want to read, among other things.
Syntax:
Get-Content -Path
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Get-Content cmdlet:
- Get-Content -Path D:\Test\sample.txt -TotalCount 10 : Read only the first ten lines of the file
- Get-Content -Path D:\Test\sample.txt -Wait : Monitor a file and display new lines as they’re added and the file is saved
Get-ChildItem
The Get-ChildItem cmdlet allows you to view all the items (files and folders) at your specified location. Running it without any parameters returns items in your current location, but you can force it to find items at other locations, too.
Syntax:
Get-ChildItem -Path
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Get-ChildItem cmdlet:
- Get-ChildItem -Path D:\Test : Find files and folders in the Test folder in the D: directory
- Get-ChildItem -Path D:\Test -Name : Get the names of files and folders at a specified location
- Get-ChildItem -Path D:\Test -Filter *.txt -Recurse : Scan a directory and its folders for all text files
Copy-Item
Copy-Item lets you copy items (files and folders) from one location to another. You just need to specify the path of the file or folder you want to move along with the path of the location where you want to move it. The copied file continues to live at the original location.
Syntax:
Copy-Item -Destination
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Copy-Item cmdlet:
- Copy-Item D:\Test\sample.txt -Destination D:\Test2\sample2.txt : Copy sample.txt file to another location with sample2.txt name
- Copy-Item D:\Test\ -Destination D:\Test2\ -Recurse : Duplicate the Test folder along with all its subfolders and files to Test2
Move-Item
Move-Item is a handy cmdlet for when you want to move an item (file or folder) from one location to another. Unlike the copy command, it doesn’t keep the item at its original location after the operation. Instead, it moves it to the new location.
Syntax:
Move-Item -Path -Destination
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Move-Item cmdlet:
- Move-Item -Path D:\Test\sample.txt -Destination D:\Test2\ : Move the sample.txt file from the Test folder to the Test2 folder
- Move-Item -Path D:\Test\sample.txt -Destination D:\Test2\sample2.txt : Move the sample.txt file to the Test2 folder and rename it to sample2.txt
- Move-Item -Path .\*.txt -Destination D:\Test2 : Move all files with the .txt extension in the current directory to Test2
Remove-Item
Remove-Item allows you to remove or delete one or more items (files and folders) from a location. Remember that this cmdlet permanently deletes the item instead of moving it to the Recycle Bin for restoration.
Syntax:
Remove-Item -Path
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Remove-Item cmdlet:
- Remove-Item -Path D:\Test*.* : Delete all files with a dot (.) in their name
- Remove-Item -Path D:\Test*.* : Delete all files with a .doc file extension in the Test folder
Set-Location
Set-Location lets you change the current working location to your specified location. It’s quite handy when you’ve to perform multiple operations on different directories.
Syntax:
Set-Location -Path
Example use cases for PowerShell’s Set-Location cmdlet:
- Set-Location -Path D: : Set the working location to the D: drive
- Set-Location -Path D: -PassThru : Set the working location to the D: drive and display that location
You Should Also Learn Command Prompt
PowerShell is just one of the many powerful tools Microsoft bundles with Windows. You also have Command Prompt (CMD) — a command-line interpreter that lets you perform various system operations using commands. If you haven’t already, be sure to check out our essential Command Prompt commands cheatsheet, as that can help you use your Windows PC more efficiently as well.

Pause for a moment and listen. What do you hear? Chances are, somewhere in the background, is the ever-present hum of a road.
More than 4.2 million miles of public roads crisscross the lower 48 states—enough to reach the Moon and back almost nine times. This vast network of roads spiderwebs its way across the contiguous US, leaving only about 5 percent as an inventoried roadless area or wilderness.
Now, some of those last remaining lands free of roads are under threat from the Trump administration’s proposed rollback of the 2001 Roadless Rule. That includes southeast Alaska’s Tongass National Forest, where eagles, bears, salmon, and many other species thrive in old-growth coastal forest along the Inside Passage.
In announcing its plan, the administration said rescinding the rule would remove prohibitions on road construction and logging on nearly 59 million acres of national forest, arguing that the rule slowed economic development. A 30-day public comment period on the formal proposal starts once it is published in the Federal Register. Instructions on how to submit comments are included in the proposal.
In Congress, another effort is underway to try to change the law through an amendment to the Wildfire Prevention Act. That change, if approved, would both remove the Roadless Rule and prevent the US Forest Service from reinstituting it in the future, despite overwhelming public support for the rule.
As ecologists who have spent decades studying wilderness and the animals and ecological functions that depend on undisturbed habitats, we believe it’s important to understand that preserving roadless areas has value for environmental health, clean water, wildlife survival and people’s own well-being.
What is the Roadless Rule?
The National Forest Roadless Area Conservation Policy, better known as the Roadless Rule, was issued in January 2001 by President Bill Clinton. It has had overwhelming public support and received more public comments than any other rule in history.
The rule prohibits road construction, maintenance and commercial timber harvest in inventoried roadless areas within the National Forest System. It applies to over 58 million acres across the country, excluding Idaho and Colorado, which have their own state-specific roadless rules. While most of these roadless areas are in the western states and Alaska, 38 total states as well as Puerto Rico host roadless areas.

There is much to be said for the extraordinary women living ordinary lives, who nonetheless shaped India. Women have changed public life in the country far more than their presence in formal politics would suggest.
And so, as India marked its 79th birthday over the weekend, I found myself reflecting on the multitude of people’s movements, big and small – as well as the women who helped shape them. During India’s struggle for freedom from British rule, women organised boycotts of British goods, made contraband salt and marched to confront the police, taking on roles usually dominated by men. In the 1970s Chipko movement, protesting deforestation, women put their bodies on the line, wrapping them around trees to stop them being felled, turning a local struggle into a national reckoning over environment and development. More recently, grandmothers in Shaheen Bagh sat to protest the citizenship law, which critics have denounced as discriminatory, creating space for dissent when many thought none existed.
Today, routes into public life for women have multiplied, with social media enabling people without political links to be in the public eye. But not all barriers have disappeared. Electoral politics remains notoriously hard to break into, especially for women. Almost half of all female parliamentarians and state legislators come from political families, while for men it is 18%, a 2025 analysis by Association for Democratic Reforms showed.
What makes a woman leading an ordinary life suddenly want to put her head above the parapet to change things for everyone? I spoke to women thrust into the spotlight in the recent student movement, who have stepped in front of vans, starved themselves and had abuse hurled at them in the process – to find out why they do it.
‘Politics is not just slogans and protests’: Neha Bora, 29
The president of the leftwing All India Students’ Association, Bora fasted for 23 days, demanding accountability over exam paper leaks and the resignation of the Education Minister during the Cockroach Protests. Now, she is touring the country as part of a Gen Z Rising outreach campaign on education reforms.
“I am a PhD student at Jawaharlal Nehru University in theatre and performance studies. My family’s political understanding is very different from mine. I ended up joining politics because that was the only way I could make sense of the times that I was living in – to not be … completely helpless in the decisions that are made for me, that should be made by me. To have a say in what I do, how I do it and what gets done around me. What is tolerable, what is good, what is injustice – all these definitions made sense to me through politics. Theatre was the first thing that taught me that politics is not just slogans and protests. Politics is the very language in which you talk to yourselves, the thoughts you formulate in your head, the relationships you have with your friends, family and peers. Student politics reaffirmed this idea.
Freedom as a student means the ability to study in a university where the model of education has not been turned into an opportunity for profit. Where education is something that helps societies move forward from dogmatism, conservatism and orthodoxy.”
‘Freedom for me is to have a voice – and not be ashamed’: Rhiya Ahir, 27
A model, actor and theatre artist from Mumbai, Ahir made the split-second decision to physically block a police van holding detained protesters – an act that exposed her to an organised hate campaign.
“I started doing theatre when I was four and a half. It taught me empathy and understanding other people’s pain, even people I don’t know. I’ve always been raised with the belief that if you see something wrong you have to step in.
Freedom for me is to have a voice, to put it across confidently and to not be ashamed. I was trolled for a photo in a swimsuit. But what about the uncles who wear chaddis at the Ganga ghat? My clothes are not my character. My clothes cannot overshadow the point or the fact that I was there, and I helped 20 students get back home safely that day. So, my clothes are just my clothes.
The hate did make me second-guess myself. The first two days [after the Mumbai protest] were very difficult because I was still trying to wrap my head around what had happened. They couldn’t find fault with my argument, so they started questioning my character. They went through my Instagram and found that I was a model. They talked about what I wear. They said she’s doing it for the camera.
When the hate started pouring in I was like, ‘What did I do to offend someone? Did I do something wrong?’ Then I realised this doesn’t change my reality. This doesn’t change who I am as a person. I don’t have to prove myself to anyone.”
‘The police have visited my ancestral village asking for information on me’: Danish Ali, 24
Ali was among the student activists on hunger strike at Jantar Mantar. A member of the Jawaharlal Nehru University student union, she faces a year-long suspension for dismantling a facial recognition system at the campus library. For her, freedom is deeply personal and rooted in her identity as a Muslim woman.
“I come from a very small town in Madhya Pradesh. No one in my family had even visited the city, so going to Delhi for higher education was almost like going abroad for education. Since the protest, the police have visited my ancestral village asking for information on me. They called my father, asking him to tell me to focus on my studies.
As a student activist, freedom means to be able to critique the government openly and say that we don’t like their policies. Freedom is being assertive about your individuality and not caring what the society would says, what your parents might say or what the state might do to you.
Freedom also means being an equal citizen in this country. Muslims in this country are being made to feel as if they are secondary and that they don’t have any right to express their religious or cultural identities. I am an equal citizen and I don’t want anyone to tell me otherwise.”
‘What used to work … won’t work with the youth’: Ratna Singh, 31
She traded a career in the law and journalism to join the Cockroach Janata party, where she now serves as the legal head. She felt drawn to the protests, seeing her work reflected in the students’ demand for accountability. Initially hesitant to become its public face, she stepped forward as spokesperson when they needed female voices.
“When I was in law school, most of my classmates would go to law chambers for internships but I would spend the summers teaching children at NGOs. Education has been something I have been very sensitive towards, and I believe every child should have access to it.
A lot of people were criticising us [and calling us] an impatient generation. We are impatient because we want to see change. We can’t be protesting and be OK with not getting answers from the government. We are also just done with divide and rule politics on the basis of religion. Political parties need to understand that what used to work for a certain mindset of people – it won’t work with the youth.
There are so many protests which have begun in different parts of the country. The fear of speaking up is gone. We are seeing a lot of leaders coming up in their own districts. They are starting their own initiatives. I think that’s giving us all hope to keep going.”
What else we’re reading about
Political promises | In his Independence Day speech, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a series of youth-focused initiatives, including an AI skills programme, free online coaching for competitive exams and a countrywide sport talent hunt. His call to identify “dimagi naxals”, or people aligned with Naxal ideology, referring to the armed guerilla movement in central India, was criticised by the Opposition as a threat to suppress critics and rivals.
Environment targets missed | The Green India Mission, for protecting and restoring the country’s declining forest cover, fell short of its target by 97% over the past decade, according to an audit report tabled in Parliament. New forest cover added was just 0.03409 million hectares, the report said, citing poor planning and inadequate funding.
Sister act | Two women of Indian origin adopted by separate Dutch families 40 years ago, who became friends as children, recently discovered they are sisters after a DNA test, Reuters reported. “It’s like a missing puzzle piece has been found,” one said.
Guest shelf
A recommendation from someone with great taste
Actor Imran Khan (@imrankhan) recommends: “Rang De Basanti is an extremely timely and relevant film for this moment; it follows a young English film-maker who befriends a group of Indian students. They set out to make a film about the Indian freedom movement. A tragic accident blurs the lines between past and present, throwing them into their own conflict against an unjust power structure. The film is funny but also heartbreaking. It celebrates the spirit of the great revolutionaries, and imagines what their modern counterparts might stand for. And the soundtrack gives us AR Rahman at his most audaciously experimental. It rocks.”

For creator Maroof Umar (@maroofculmen), storytelling can change the way we see the world. And the stories he tells, rooted in heritage and culture through cinematically shot videos, can both break and mend your heart. Each has a person at its center but the stories also belong to the city and its communities. Texas did reinstate rules that treat certain THC products as controlled substances.
Texas did not make all marijuana possession a felony; possession of 2 ounces or less of marijuana remains a Class B misdemeanor, for example. In addition, the vote was a Democratic primary proposition, not a statewide legalization referendum open to all voters.
In late July and August 2026, social media users circulated a claim that Texas made marijuana a felony after more than 70% of voters supported legalizing it.
"Texas just made weed a felony after over 70% of voters voted to legalize it. That's what happens when incarceration rates go down and for-profit prisons start to lose money," one Threads post (archived) read.
(Threads user @bigmike_muckenthaler)
The rumor spread on multiple social media platforms, including Instagram, LinkedIn, Bluesky, X and Facebook.
In short, it's not true that Texas voters approved marijuana legalization in a statewide referendum, as social media posts suggested. In reality, voters taking part in the Democratic primary election in March 2026 were asked whether they supported legalizing cannabis for adults. The question appeared as a "survey" on Democratic primary ballots and was a nonbinding party proposition.
Also, Texas did not make all marijuana possession a felony. The change that took effect July 31, 2026, reinstated definitions under which manufactured delta-8 THC and certain other forms of THC were designated controlled substances. Possession of some of these products can result in felony charges. However, possession of 2 ounces or less of marijuana remains a Class B misdemeanor under Texas law. Moreover, the change didn't originate with the vote in 2026. The disputed THC definitions dated back to 2021 and were reinstated in 2026 after several years of court proceedings.
As such, we have rated this claim as mostly false.
The vote was a Democratic primary proposition
The first part of the claim referred to a proposition that appeared on Democratic primary ballots on March 3, 2026. An official Harris County sample ballot identified it as "DEM - PROPOSITION 8" and asked voters whether "Texas should legalize cannabis for adults and automatically expunge criminal records for past low-level cannabis offenses." Respondents could choose "for" or "against."
The proposition received strong support. Official statewide results showed 80.1% in favor and 19.9% against. However, this was not a statewide referendum in which Texas voters decided to legalize marijuana. The question appeared on Democratic primary ballots only, and the result did not change state law.
Under Texas law, political parties can place nonbinding propositions (such as cannabis legalization) on their primary ballots. The process is described in the Texas Election Code, which allows a political party's state executive committee to put a proposal on the primary ballot about specific legislation or another issue that could be included in the party's platform or resolutions.
In other words, the cannabis question was not a statewide legalization referendum open to all Texas voters, but a nonbinding proposition presented statewide to Democratic primary voters. As such, the vote did not legalize marijuana or change Texas criminal law.
Texas did not make all weed possession a felony
The second part of the claim referred to restrictions on certain THC products that took effect July 31, 2026. According to the Texas Department of State Health Services, the change reinstated rules treating manufactured delta-8 THC and some other forms of THC as controlled substances.
Possession of certain controlled THC substances can carry felony penalties, but this did not mean Texas made all marijuana possession a felony. Under Texas law, possession of two ounces or less of marijuana remains a Class B misdemeanor, while larger amounts can carry more-serious penalties. Texas also continues to permit up to 0.3% delta-9 THC in consumable hemp products.
THC policy at issue dated from 2021
The policy at issue actually dated back several years. According to the Texas Supreme Court's May 2026 decision, DSHS published the disputed schedules in 2021, seeking to treat manufactured delta-8 THC as a controlled substance.
Hemp businesses challenged the policy, and a court temporarily blocked it while the case continued. On May 1, 2026, the Texas Supreme Court ruled that state law did not prevent DSHS from classifying manufactured delta-8 THC as a controlled substance and reversed the injunction.
Following the ruling, DSHS reinstated the disputed definitions, effective July 31, 2026. The reinstated definitions are now facing a separate federal court challenge. On Aug. 9, a federal judge denied an emergency request to temporarily block the restrictions, while a request for a preliminary injunction remained pending. Therefore, although the Democratic primary vote happened in March and the restrictions took effect in July, the disputed policy dated back to 2021.
Bottom line
All in all, the claim had a kernel of truth. Democratic primary voters supported a nonbinding proposition calling for the legalization of cannabis, and possession of certain controlled THC products in Texas can lead to felony charges. However, Texas voters didn't legalize marijuana and Texas didn't later make all marijuana possession a felony. Finally, the THC policy at issue dated back to 2021 — several years before the 2026 vote.

The score is Machines 1-0 Humans - at least when it comes to predicting football results, anyway.
AI - in this case Microsoft chatbot CoPilot - finished top of the BBC predictions league at the first attempt last season, but will it stay there?
BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton, his guests and the BBC readers will be hoping to strike back, and land a blow for the human race.
"It was a final-day defeat for me, that is how close I came to the title," Sutton said.
"But I keep reading how AI models are going rogue and attacking each other.
"So, was I hacked too? It sounds like cheating to me - if so, then last season should really go down as a victory for me."
Who will win this time? Sutton is again making predictions for all 380 Premier League games this season, against AI, BBC Sport readers and a variety of guests.

Chris Sutton and Liam Fray were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

Holding simultaneous elections for the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies in 2029 under the Modi government's ‘One Nation, One Election’ initiative is possible if the Constitution is amended and state governments support the move, according to P.P. Chaudhary, the chairman of the joint parliamentary panel examining the related bills.
The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, which aim to synchronise Lok Sabha and State Assembly polls, were sent to the 31-member joint committee of Parliament headed by Mr. Chaudhary, a BJP MP from Rajasthan, following the Opposition's demand for broader scrutiny.
When asked if State assembly elections could be held alongside the 2029 Lok Sabha polls, Mr. Chaudhary said on Monday (August 24, 2026) that if the constitutional amendment is approved in Parliament by 2028, the rollout of ‘One Nation, One Election’ can begin that same year.
"Then what is the problem? If the States express their desire in 2029, we can't give the States directions to dissolve their Assembly.”
"They have to make their own decisions. It depends on the respective Chief Ministers and their Council of Ministers. If the Council of Ministers of the States decide in favour of ‘One Nation One Election’, that State elections should be held along with the Lok Sabha polls, then it is possible. It is up to them what they decide. The Indian Constitution allows that; it is permissible.”
"Under the Indian Constitution, the states are empowered to hold simultaneous polls," he told reporters at the Parliament House complex after a meeting of the panel.
The BJP leader said democracy means the will of the people, not the will of the political parties, and everyone has to see what the will of the people is.
"We have visited 10 states and interacted with a cross-section of people, and we have realised that 99 per cent of people, civil society, want simultaneous polls for Lok Sabha and State Mssemblies," he said.
Mr. Chaudhary said there may be different opinions of political parties, but the committee has to work together in the interest of the country.
"We have to work on what the people want, what the country wants. We are working with the will of the people. That is why we have invited civil society members to take their opinions," he said.
Mr. Chaudhary said that Parliament gave the panel the mandate to examine and give recommendations on the two Constitution amendment bills.
Two-thirds of members of Parliament have to support the bills for their passage.
Another government-sponsored Constitution amendment bill, the delimitation-linked women reservation bill, which also required support of two-thirds of members of Parliament, was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April.
Mr. Chaudhary said the Parliament mandated the committee to examine the legislation and fix the shortcomings, if any, and make sure that the simultaneous polls are held successfully.
He said if simultaneous elections in Lok Sabha and State assemblies are held, everyone will benefit from it and the biggest beneficiary will be the country's youth.
mr. Chaudhary also said that 30% of the time of government schools is used in poll-related work every year.
The Bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024, following which they were referred to the joint committee for examination.
The Bills were formulated after a high-level panel, headed by former President Ram Nath Kovind, recommended holding Lok Sabha, State assembly and local body elections simultaneously in a phased manner. Union Home Minister Amit Shah was also a member of the high-level panel headed by Mr. Kovind.
Following the adoption of the Constitution, elections to the Lok Sabha and all State Legislative Assemblies were conducted simultaneously from 1951 to 1967.
The first general elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies were held together in 1951-52, a practice that continued for three subsequent general elections in 1957, 1962, and 1967.
However, this cycle of synchronised elections was disrupted in 1968 and 1969 due to the premature dissolution of some State Legislative Assemblies.
The Fourth Lok Sabha was also dissolved prematurely in 1970, with fresh elections held in 1971. Unlike the First, Second, and Third Lok Sabha, which completed their full five-year terms, the Fifth Lok Sabha's term was extended until 1977 under Article 352 because of the declaration of Emergency.
Since then, only a few Lok Sabha terms have lasted the full five years, such as the Eighth, Tenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth. Others, including the Sixth, Seventh, Ninth, Eleventh, Twelfth, and Thirteenth, were dissolved early.
State Assemblies have faced similar disruptions over the years. Premature dissolutions and term extensions have become a recurring challenge.
These developments have firmly disrupted the cycle of simultaneous elections, leading to the current pattern of staggered electoral schedules across the country.

The best way to test your Dolby Atmos sound system
Pick a good benchmark video, and stick with it.
Immersive, cinema-grade audio at home isn't impossible, but getting it right can be a labor of love. Setting up a Dolby Atmos sound system, for instance, requires careful speaker placement and plenty of fine-tuning for the best results. If it's done right, the audio should feel like it's coming from all around you.
The only problem is knowing how to test it, because you can't just hook it up and assume everything will sound right in your room. Once you've checked each speaker is working properly, you'll need to put the entire system through its paces to check that you're getting the full Dolby Atmos experience.
Test each speaker with the official Dolby Atmos test file
You've installed your Dolby Atmos sound system. Before you settle down for a movie, you're going to want to perform some technical testing first. To be clear, this isn't going to be a test of how good your system sounds. It isn't necessarily calibrated, and you'll probably need to make further tweaks and changes.
What it is, however, is a test run of each component in your Atmos setup. Dolby's official 7.1.4 channel test file lets you test whether each speaker and audio channel is working as expected. This'll let you check your speakers are working properly, with clean audio and no dropouts. It can also be used with smaller Atmos setups, such as 5.1.2, although the test includes channels that those systems don't have. Those channels may just stay silent, or it may sound like it's coming from a different speaker than the file suggests, depending on your config.
It's also an immersion test. If your setup is working correctly, each test signal will match to a specific speaker and correspond to a different audio channel. As the channel test works through each speaker, you should be able to pinpoint where it's coming from, matching up to what the test file is telling you. For instance, if the speaker tells you that it's playing from the left top rear, it should sound like it's coming from there.
The test file is a video, so you'll see a visual guide to explain which speaker should be sounding. If you've placed a speaker in the wrong place, this'll give you a chance to swap it out. You can also correct any wrongly-assigned channels to speakers in your settings, if needed.
The official Dolby Atmos 7.1.4 channel test file is available to download from Dolby's website. Third-party alternatives also exist online with different audio mixes to try out, too. Once you've tested the setup and you're confident that it's technically working, you can move onto trying it out with some real content.
Use a short movie or song as a benchmark to stress test your setup
At this point, each speaker should be working, so the next test is to try playing real content you'd listen to that has been mixed for Dolby Atmos. You'll only know from playing real content, like movies you watch or songs you listen to, if the immersive experience you're expecting is right or not.
You can sit for a full-length movie but, realistically, that isn't a good test. You'll want a brief sequence that you can watch and replay, repeatedly, while you make adjustments. It'll give you a benchmark to refer back to with each change you make. Once you have that, you can make adjustments to your setup to improve the audio.
Sol Levante is a short anime film produced by Netflix that's perfect for this. It's under five minutes long, so you can replay it again and again. More importantly, it makes use of an extensive Dolby Atmos spatial audio mix that works as a stress test for your setup. The audio playback features movements and positional effects to help you test how accurately your system places sounds around and above you.
There are a couple of things you'll want to listen out for as the movie plays. Volume is important, but for Dolby Atmos, spatial awareness is the greater priority. Audio that moves around on-screen should move throughout your speakers, with dialogue that stays anchored and clear at the front. Any ambient effects should help give you that immersive feel of a space greater than just the screen, filling the entire room around you from top to bottom.
The whole point of Dolby Atmos audio is for you to feel like you're experiencing three-dimensional audio. If Sol Levante sounds right, you can move onto a bigger test, like a full-blown movie. Just be sure that you stick to a benchmark if you want to make further tweaks. It could be a key point in the film with a few minutes of variation in the audio, for instance, that you replay again and again to get your setup sounding right.
You can also use other types of content, like music through Apple Music, to test Dolby Atmos. For the full Dolby Atmos experience, however, you'll need an Apple TV 4K connected via HDMI to your kit. The important thing here is picking songs with obvious spatial effects, with a good set of vocals, instruments and effects throughout. It helps if it's music that you listen to regularly, as you'll have a better feel for how the music should sound in your room.
Double-check your settings and connections
Your Dolby Atmos setup should sound clear and well calibrated by this point. If it doesn't, there are several points in the chain that you can double check to fix any problems.
The source might be the issue itself. Make sure that the movie or song that you're playing is made for Dolby Atmos, meaning it has Dolby Atmos audio available for playback, rather than standard 5.1 surround or stereo. The streaming service you're watching and the playback device itself need to support Atmos content, too.
It's never a bad idea to double-check all of your connections, either. Start with your individual speakers and subwoofer, but also check the link between your playback devices and your sound system. HDMI ARC or eARC is probably the right call here, as it lets your TV pass Dolby Atmos audio through to your sound system.
You can also double-check your speaker assignments and calibration settings. Starting again with the Dolby test if you're concerned about this is probably the way to go. A speaker might work fine but have the wrong channel applied, or be in the wrong position for your room and require adjustment.
Once the technical tests are complete, pick your benchmark and stick to it. Whether it's Sol Levante or something else, keep it short and sweet, and play it back each time you make a change to your settings or setup. With any luck, a few small tweaks will get your audio sounding exactly right.

A coalition of former internationals — among them World Cup winners and FIFA Legends — has demanded urgent reforms at FIFA, accusing the organisation’s leadership under President Gianni Infantino of being intoxicated by power.
Infantino faces growing calls to step down after dropping a plan to set up a commercial arm for FIFA tournament rights and sell a 20 per cent stake to private investors. Despite open resistance from several of FIFA’s own confederations, including UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, and talk of a possible no-confidence motion, the Swiss official has given no indication he will leave the role he has held since 2016.
“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” said former players including France’s 1998 men’s World Cup winners Emmanuel Petit, Bixente Lizarazu and Robert Pires as well as American former women’s world champion Briana Scurry and former England international Lucy Bronze.
“Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under FIFA’s current leadership. Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football,” the group said.
ALSO READ: Samuel Eto’o urges support for embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino
The group also features ex-Peru striker Claudio Pizarro, former Argentina midfielder Juan Sebastian Veron, ex-Togo captain Emmanuel Adebayor, and FIFA Legends Didier Drogba and David James. FIFA Legends are former players honoured for their contributions to the sport who represent the global body at exhibition matches and back social and charity initiatives worldwide.
“We call on all stakeholders to step forward and help reshape the future of our sport. There are good people within FIFA who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structural change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run,” the group said.
Infantino is due to face re-election next year, but senior figures told Reuters last week that FIFA’s regional power blocs are weighing up whether to bring forward a no-confidence vote before the ballot.
“Those who step onto the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together. For the fans, for the players, and for the good of the game, we will be silent no more,” the players’ group said.

Taiwan reportedly indicted NVIDIA employees for exporting prohibited AI servers to China
The nine individuals are accused of 'severely damaged our nation's image,' prosecutors said.
Although the US has relaxed its restrictions on NVIDIA AI chip exports to China, illegal exports apparently still take place. Prosecutors in Taiwan just indicted nine individuals, including NVIDIA and Super Micro employees, for illegally bringing AI servers into China, Reuters reported.
The defendants "colluded with one another at various levels for enormous profit, illegally exporting high-end servers, increasing corporate compliance costs, and severely damaging our nation's international image," prosecutors from the northern city of Keelung said in a statement. They did this, the team added, despite being "fully aware" of NVIDIA and Super Micro's "rigorous" export control procedures.
Although NVIDIA is an American company, most of its chips are manufactured by the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world's largest chip maker by far. TSMC's latest Blackwell AI chips are manufactured in Phoenix, Arizona, but are still shipped to Taiwan for advanced packaging prior to final assembly.
The US has banned the sale of cutting-edge AI tech from NVIDIA and others to China since 2022. Recently, it has allowed sales to China of previous-generation products like H200 chips that are several years old. Taiwan is ultra-strict about exports of newer technology, lest it displease US regulators and, in particular, the Trump administration.
Despite Taiwan's clampdown, bad actors have found ways to get such chips into China. In one instance, $1 billion worth of server racks may have been shipped through Southeast Asian countries like Thailand or Malaysia to circumvent US export controls. In another case, the US charged three people with allegedly exporting $3.5 billion worth of AI servers to China, again by routing them through third-party countries.
